newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-PARSONS AND MADDY LIFT CHAMPIONS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PARSONS AND MADDY LIFT CHAMPIONS.

text.p: Middlesex's hopes of beating English county champions Leicestershire were jolted as the old and the new combined to spearhead a fightback by the title-holders on Friday.
Gordon Parsons, the 37-year-old seamer, took Middlesex's last four wickets for just five runs in 26 balls at Lord's as the home side were restricted to a first-innings lead of 115.
Then 23-year-old opener Darren Maddy wiped out that advantage with a brilliant 103 as Leicestershire ended the third day with their second innings on 236 for three -- 121 ahead.
Fellow opener Vince Wells, who played the anchor role in a stand of 173 with Maddy, was still there unbeaten on 76.
Across London at The Oval, Surrey bowled themselves in with an outside chance of victory against Essex, and must score a further 300 with eight wickets left on the last day on Saturday.
Essex looked set to hoist a daunting target with Adrian Grayson hitting 105 and Graham Gooch 56 as they cruised to 223 for three in their second innings.
But they then lost five wickets for 28 runs and were bowled out for 302 to leave Surrey chasing 370 to win. The home side were 70 for two at the close.
Pace pair Simon Brown and Alan Walker set up the possibility of a rare championship victory for Durham as they shone with both bat and ball against Sussex at Chester-le-Street.
The last-wicket pair shared a stand of 41, Brown hitting 24 and Walker 14 not out, as Durham posted 338 in their first innings to trail by 35.
Then Brown claimed three for 55 and Walker four for 61 as Sussex were restricted to a second-innings total of 243 for eight at the close, a lead of 278.
England discard Robin Smith smashed his first century of the season to lead a Hampshire fightback against Derbyshire at Chesterfield.
Smith's 154 included 23 fours and two sixes as Hampshire replied to the home side's first-innings 523 with 422 for seven.
